To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the conceptual system is spatially grounded and that this is why the spatial domain is privileged.

the conceptual system is spatially grounded, that spatial descriptions are the basis for the development of concepts, that spatial information is the first information acquired by the conceptual system, that spatial descriptions of the world are the first language learned by the child, that spatial descriptions provide a basis for explicit preverbal thoughts, and that concepts of emotions, color, and theory mind are acquired much later than spatial concepts.

(i) the spatial primitives are the foundation of the conceptual system; (ii) the conceptual system is enriched by associating the spatial primitives with bodily feelings; (iii) this enrichment leads to the acquisition of concepts for emotions, sensory qualities, and theory of the mind; and (iv) the conceptual system of infants is similar to that of nonhuman primates.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the nature and origins of conceptual structure.
the origins of concepts, the nature of conceptual structure, and the role of conceptual structure in language acquisition.
how conceptual systems are built, the role of the conceptual system in thought, and how conceptual systems are related to language.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the spatial domain is the foundation for the conceptual system and that all other concepts are built upon it.
the conceptual system is founded in the spatial domain, and its enrichment comes from the addition of concepts of emotions, sensations, and theory of the mind.
spatial descriptions form the core of conceptual thought, which is the foundation for language, and that the conceptual system is the basis for the human mind and the human condition.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have a single theory that can account for the entire development of concepts from infancy through adulthood, and that it can account for the similarities and differences in the conceptual systems of humans and nonhuman primats.
we propose that concepts are spatially based, and that the spatial primitives of the conceptual system can be identified.
we have a theory that explains the spatial basis of conceptualization and how it is enriched.
The main takeaway from our work is that
spatial concepts are the foundation of the conceptual system.
the conceptual system is grounded in spatial information and that this grounding is essential for the development of conceptual knowledge.
the conceptual system begins with spatial descriptions of the environment and that these are enriched by the incorporation of information from other domains.
